common_name: Genie Magnolia (Compact Deep Purple Reblooming Hybrid Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown or balled-and-burlapped trees in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Genie flowers at a young age and stays compact, making it well suited to smaller residential landscapes.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade. Bred in New Zealand from the same breeding lines that produced 'Vulcan' and 'Black Tulip', Genie carries thick-petaled, goblet-shaped flowers in an exceptionally deep purple-maroon, nearly black in bud, that stay cupped rather than opening flat. It blooms heavily in spring on bare branches and then reblooms sporadically through summer, giving a much longer season of color than most magnolias. The tree grows with a dense, narrow, upright habit that fits tight garden spaces far better than larger saucer magnolia cultivars. Water deeply during establishment and mulch to conserve soil moisture.

common_name: Star Wars Magnolia (Large Pink-Flowered Campbellii Hybrid Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown or balled-and-burlapped trees in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun, sheltered from strong wind and late frost pockets; Star Wars needs a sheltered site since it blooms relatively early on bare wood.

directions: Plant in moist, fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun, sheltered from strong wind. Bred in New Zealand by Felix Jury from Magnolia campbellii stock, Star Wars produces enormous, fragrant, deep pink flowers up to 10 to 12 inches across on bare branches in early to mid spring, with a notably long bloom period and sporadic rebloom later in the season. Its glossy, semi-evergreen foliage persists later into the year than most deciduous magnolias, adding extra garden presence. The tree grows vigorously into a large, broad-canopied specimen, so give it plenty of room and a sheltered site away from cold air drainage to protect the early flowers from late frost damage.

planting.note: Plant container-grown or balled-and-burlapped trees in spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Sunsation flowers as the leaves emerge, which helps protect its blooms from late spring frosts.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade. Bred by hybridizer August Kehr, Sunsation produces large, upright, tulip-shaped flowers in a soft buttery yellow with a faint blush at the base, opening as the foliage begins to unfurl in mid spring, which helps the blooms escape the late frosts that can damage earlier-flowering yellow magnolias. It grows with a strong, upright, pyramidal habit into a substantial specimen tree well suited as a focal point. Water deeply during the first several growing seasons and mulch to keep roots cool and moist.

common_name: Alba Superba Magnolia (Fragrant White Upright Saucer Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown or balled-and-burlapped trees in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Alba Superba blooms somewhat later than Alexandrina, giving some protection from late frost damage.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Alba Superba is a white-flowered saucer magnolia cultivar producing goblet-shaped, lightly fragrant blooms that open pure white with only a faint blush at the base, opening on bare branches in mid spring. It grows with a more upright, tidy habit than many saucer magnolia cultivars, developing into a small tree or large multi-stemmed shrub with minimal pruning needs beyond removing dead or crossing wood. Established trees are long-lived, low-maintenance landscape specimens, though a late hard freeze can still brown open flowers in an unusually cold spring.

common_name: Lennei Alba Magnolia (Full-Petaled White Saucer Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown or balled-and-burlapped trees in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Lennei Alba blooms somewhat later than Alexandrina, giving it some protection from late-season frost damage.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; Lennei Alba is a white-flowered form of the classic 'Lennei' saucer magnolia, producing the same unusually full, heavy-petaled, goblet-shaped blooms but in creamy ivory-white rather than rose-purple. It flowers on bare branches in mid spring and grows into a broad, spreading, multi-stemmed small tree or large shrub, needing little pruning beyond removing dead or crossing wood. Established trees are vigorous, long-lived landscape specimens, though a late hard freeze can still brown open flowers in an unusually cold spring.
